cards.text: Meet Micah the Moreshite. The word of the LORD comes to him in the days of THREE kings of Judah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, and what he sees is about Samaria and Jerusalem. Three kings and he's still on the job, while I worked ONE kitchen and got slid into a junk drawer.
This message doesn't ease in. No small talk, it opens LOUD, like a phone alarm at 5 a.m. with the volume ALL the way up.

cards.question: The message calls all peoples to hear, and the whole ___ to listen.

cards.text: Then it says, "May the Lord GOD bear witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple." Witness AGAINST you, friend, and that is NOT a glowing job reference.
And behold, the LORD comes forth from His dwelling place, and He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth. Trust me, friend, nobody's hitting snooze on THAT alarm.

cards.question: When the LORD comes down and treads on the high places of the earth, what will the mountains beneath Him do?
While the mountains melt beneath the LORD, what does the message say will happen to the valleys?
Melting mountains and splitting valleys. The message says all this is because of what?

cards.text: Then it asks what the transgression of Jacob is, and points right at a city: "Is it not Samaria?" Then it asks about the high place of Judah: "Is it not Jerusalem?"

Next the message says Samaria will be made a heap of rubble in the open field, with her stones poured into the valley and her foundations exposed. That's not a remodel, friend, that's the whole house down to the dirt.

cards.question: Once Samaria is rubble in the open field, what does the message say the spot will become?

answers.text: A planting area for a vineyard
A pasture for flocks of sheep
A camp for an army of soldiers

cards.question: Along with the city itself, the message says all of Samaria's ___ will be destroyed.

cards.text: ALL of Samaria's carved images will be smashed to pieces, and ALL her wages burned in the fire. Then it says, "Since she collected the wages of a prostitute, they will be used again on a prostitute."

cards.question: Right after the word against Samaria, the next line is a cry of grief: "Because of this I will lament and wail…"

cards.text: The line goes on: "I will walk barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich." Then it says her wound is incurable, and I think this one hurts.

cards.question: The message says Samaria's wound stops before it ever reaches Judah.

cards.text: Now the lament goes town by town, from Gath to Adullam, like a roll call where nobody wants to hear their name. One town is told to roll in the dust, and another to depart in shameful nakedness. Calamity came down from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem, and Lachish is called the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion. Then comes word to send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath.

cards.question: The lament ends with a command: shave yourselves bald and cut off your hair. Why?

answers.text: To keep a vow to the LORD

cards.question: Here's the reason for all that mourning: the precious children will go into ___.
